title: Notes on Numerical Integration of ODEs

contract.reader: An engineer or student with calculus and Taylor series who has an ODE to simulate, often arriving from a series entry that needs time-stepping background
contract.problem: Choosing a method and step size, and understanding why a step that looks accurate enough can still make a simulation blow up
contract.outcome: State and measure the order of explicit Euler and RK4; compare them at equal cost; find the largest stable step for a mode from the amplification factor and stability region; tell accuracy from stability; know when to turn to implicit methods
contract.contribution: One short page that keeps accuracy and stability apart on the test equation, with order derived, measured by a runnable script and compared at equal work, and stability regions including the imaginary axis; the common reference for the site's simulation, control and DSP entries
contract.evidence: Derivation on the test equation; standard-library Python script with output table; Butcher (2016), Hairer, Nørsett and Wanner (1993), LeVeque (2007)
contract.limitations: Fixed step only; linear analysis; stiffness and implicit methods left to the Numerical Simulation series; nonlinear order proof left to the references
